summary: If korbanos got mixed up with animals that may not be used at all, they all must die. If they got mixed with animals that may not be offered, they graze until they get a blemish, are sold, and he buys new korbanos with the money.

chunks.en: All korbanos that got mixed up with chatas animals that are left to die,
chunks.st: All the offerings that were intermingled with animals from which deriving benefit is forbidden, e.g., sin offerings left to die,

words.note: Some chatas animals may not be offered and are left to die.

chunks.en: or with an ox that must be stoned,
chunks.st: or with an ox that was sentenced to be stoned,

words.note: An ox that killed a person, which Beis Din sentenced to stoning.

chunks.en: even one in ten thousand,
chunks.st: even if the ratio is one in ten thousand,

chunks.en: all of them must die.
chunks.st: deriving benefit from them all is prohibited and they all must die.

chunks.en: If they got mixed up with an ox that was used for a sin,
chunks.st: If the offerings were intermingled with animals whose sacrifice is forbidden but deriving benefit from them is not, the halakha is different. Examples of this are an ox with which a transgression was performed, which disqualifies it from being sacrificed as an offering,

chunks.en: or that killed a person
chunks.st: or an ox that is known to have killed a person

chunks.en: by the word of one witness,
chunks.st: based on the testimony of one witness

chunks.en: or by the word of the owner,
chunks.st: or based on the admission of the owner.
chunks.stMore: Had two witnesses testified, deriving benefit from the ox would have been prohibited.

chunks.en: or with animals used in a forbidden act,
chunks.st: Additional examples include when an offering is intermingled with an animal that copulated with a person; or an animal that was the object of bestiality;

words.en: with an animal used in a forbidden act
and with an animal used in a forbidden act

chunks.en: or set aside for avodah zarah, or worshipped,
chunks.st: or with an animal that was set aside for idol worship; or one that was worshipped as a deity;

words.note: Set aside to be offered to an idol.
Treated as an idol.

chunks.en: or given as a forbidden payment, or traded for a dog,
chunks.st: or with an animal that was given as payment to a prostitute or as the price
chunks.stMore: of a dog, as it is written: “You shall not bring the payment of a harlot, or the price of a dog, into the house of the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 23:19).

words.note: An animal given as payment for something forbidden.
An animal traded for a dog.

chunks.en: or born of two kinds mixed, or a treifah,
chunks.st: Additional examples include an offering that was intermingled with an animal born of a mixture of diverse kinds, e.g., the offspring of a ram and a goat, or with an animal with a wound that will cause it to die within twelve months [tereifa],

words.note: Born from two different kinds of animals.

chunks.en: or born by a cut in the side,
chunks.st: or with an animal born by caesarean section.

words.note: Born by an operation, not in the normal way.

chunks.en: they should graze until they get a blemish,
chunks.st: In all these cases the animals that are intermingled shall graze until they become unfit for sacrifice and

words.note: A mum, which makes it not fit to be a korban.

chunks.en: and be sold, and he brings with the money of the best one
chunks.st: then they shall be sold. And from the money received in the sale, the owner shall bring another offering of the monetary value of the highest-quality

chunks.en: among them a korban of that same kind.
chunks.st: animal among them, of the same type
chunks.stMore: of offering that the intermingled offering was. The mishna continues:

chunks.en: If it got mixed up with regular animals without a blemish,
chunks.st: If sacrificial animals were intermingled with unblemished, non-sacred animals, which, if consecrated, are fit for sacrifice,

chunks.en: the regular animals should be sold to people who need that kind of korban.
chunks.st: the non-sacred animals shall be sold for the purpose of purchasing offerings of the same type as the offering with which they were intermingled.

summary: If korbanos of the same kind got mixed up, each is offered for whoever owns it. If different kinds got mixed up, they graze until they get a blemish, and he buys new korbanos. A chatas and an asham do not get mixed up.

chunks.en: Korbanos with korbanos, one kind with the same kind,
chunks.st: In a case where sacrificial animals were intermingled with other sacrificial animals, if it was an animal of one type of offering with animals of the same type of offering,

chunks.en: this one is offered for whoever owns it,
chunks.st: one shall sacrifice this animal for the sake of whoever is

chunks.en: and that one is offered for whoever owns it.
chunks.st: its owner and one shall sacrifice that animal for the sake of whoever is its owner, and both fulfill their obligation.

chunks.en: Korbanos with korbanos,
chunks.st: In a case where sacrificial animals were intermingled with other sacrificial animals,

chunks.en: one kind with a different kind,
chunks.st: where an animal of one type of offering was intermingled with animals not of the same type
chunks.stMore: of offering, e.g., two rams, where one is designated as a burnt offering and one as a peace offering,

chunks.en: they should graze until they get a blemish,
chunks.st: they shall graze until they become unfit

chunks.he: וְיִמָּכְרוּ, וְיָבִיא בִדְמֵי הַיָּפֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן מִמִּין זֶה,
chunks.en: and be sold, and he brings with the money of the best one a korban of this kind,
chunks.st: for sacrifice and then they shall be sold. And from the money received in the sale, the owner shall bring another offering of the monetary value of the highest-quality animal among them as this type of offering,

chunks.en: and with the money of the best one a korban of that kind,
chunks.st: and another offering of the monetary value of the highest-quality animal among them as that type of offering,

chunks.en: and he loses the extra money from his own pocket.
chunks.st: and he will lose the additional expense of purchasing two highest-quality animals, when he had sold only one highest-quality animal, from his own assets.

chunks.en: If they got mixed up with a bechor or with maaser,
chunks.st: In a case where sacrificial animals were intermingled with a firstborn offering or with an animal tithe offering,

chunks.en: they should graze until they get a blemish,
chunks.st: they shall graze until they become unfit

chunks.en: and be eaten like a bechor or like maaser.
chunks.st: for sacrifice and they shall both be eaten as a firstborn offering or as an animal tithe offering.

chunks.en: All korbanos can get mixed up,
chunks.st: All offerings can become indistinguishably intermingled with each other,

chunks.en: except for the chatas and the asham.
chunks.st: except for a sin offering and a guilt offering, as the Gemara will explain.

summary: If an asham got mixed up with a shelamim, Rabbi Shimon says both are shechted in the north and eaten by the stricter rules. The Sages say we may not make a korban become pasul on purpose. But mixed-up pieces of meat are eaten by the stricter rules.

chunks.he: אָשָׁם שֶׁנִּתְעָרֵב בִּשְׁלָמִים, יִרְעוּ עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֲבוּ.
chunks.en: An asham that got mixed up with a shelamim should graze until they get a blemish.
chunks.st: In the case of a guilt offering that was intermingled with a peace offering,

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: both of them should be shechted in the north,
chunks.st: Both of them should be slaughtered in the north
chunks.stMore: of the Temple courtyard, as a guilt offering must be slaughtered in the north while a peace offering may be slaughtered anywhere in the courtyard.

chunks.en: and eaten by the rules of the stricter one.
chunks.st: And they both must be eaten in accordance with the halakha of the more stringent of them,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the guilt offering, with the following halakhot: They may be eaten only in the courtyard rather than throughout Jerusalem; by male priests and not by any ritually pure Jew; and on the day they were sacrificed and the following night, and not on the day they were sacrificed, the following day, and the intervening night.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to
chunks.stMore: Rabbi Shimon: One may not limit the time of the consumption of an offering,

chunks.en: we do not bring korbanos into becoming pasul.
chunks.st: as one may not bring sacrificial animals to the status of unfitness.
chunks.stMore: According to Rabbi Shimon’s opinion, the peace offering becomes leftover, notar, the morning after it is sacrificed, and not at the end of that day, as is the halakha concerning peace offerings. Rather, the owner shall wait until these animals become blemished, redeem them, and bring an offering of each type that is worth the monetary value of the higher-quality animal among them. The mishna adds: Even according to the opinion of the Rabbis,

words.note: A shelamim eaten by the rules of an asham may end up left over too long.

chunks.en: If pieces got mixed up with pieces,
chunks.st: if pieces of the meat of one offering were intermingled with pieces of the meat of another offering, e.g.,

chunks.en: pieces of the holiest korbanos with less holy korbanos,
chunks.st: meat from offerings of the most sacred order with meat from offerings of lesser sanctity;

chunks.he: הַנֶּאֱכָלִין לְיוֹם אֶחָד בַּנֶּאֱכָלִים לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים,
chunks.en: those eaten for one day with those eaten for two days,
chunks.st: or if pieces of meat from offerings eaten for one day and the following night were intermingled with pieces of meat from offerings eaten for two days and one night,
chunks.stMore: since in that case the remedy with regard to offerings that were intermingled cannot be implemented,

chunks.en: they are eaten by the rules of the stricter one.
chunks.st: they both must be eaten in accordance with the halakha of the more stringent of them.

summary: If parts of a chatas got mixed with parts of an olah, Rabbi Eliezer says to put them all on the mizbeach and think of the chatas meat as wood. The Sages say to wait until they spoil and then burn them.

chunks.en: Parts of a chatas that got mixed up with parts of an olah,
chunks.st: In the case of the limbs of a sin offering, which are eaten by priests and may not be burned on the altar, that were intermingled with the limbs of a burnt offering, which are burned on the altar,

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: he should put them up above,
chunks.st: The priest shall place all the limbs above, on the altar,

words.note: On top of the mizbeach.

chunks.en: and I look at the chatas meat
chunks.st: and I view the flesh of the limbs of the sin offering

chunks.en: up above as if it were wood.
chunks.st: above on the altar as though they are pieces of wood burned on the altar, and not as though they are an offering.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: they should wait until they spoil, and then go out to the place of burning.
chunks.st: One should wait until the form of all the intermingled limbs decays and they will all go out to the place of burning
chunks.stMore: in the Temple courtyard, where all disqualified offerings of the most sacred order are burned.

words.note: Until the meat spoils.

summary: If parts of kosher korbanos got mixed with parts of blemished animals, Rabbi Eliezer says that once one head was offered, all the heads may be offered. The Sages say even if all but one were offered, they must be burned.

chunks.en: Parts with parts of blemished animals,
chunks.st: In a case where limbs of burnt offerings fit for sacrifice were intermingled with limbs of blemished burnt offerings,

words.note: Animals with a mum, which may not be offered.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says: Although all the limbs are unfit for sacrifice,

chunks.en: if the head of one of them was offered,
chunks.st: if the head of one of them was sacrificed

chunks.en: all the heads should be offered.
chunks.st: all the heads shall be sacrificed,
chunks.stMore: as the head that was sacrificed is assumed to have been that of the unfit animal in the mixture. Likewise,

chunks.en: If the leg of one of them was offered,
chunks.st: if one sacrificed the legs of one of them

chunks.en: all the legs should be offered.
chunks.st: all the legs shall be sacrificed.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: אֲפִלּוּ קָרְבוּ כֻלָּם חוּץ מֵאַחַד מֵהֶן,
chunks.en: even if all of them were offered except for one of them,
chunks.st: Even if all the limbs were sacrificed except for one of them,
chunks.stMore: there is a concern that the remaining limb is the unfit limb, which may not be sacrificed. Rather,

chunks.en: it must go out to the place of burning.
chunks.st: all of the limbs must go out to the place of burning in the Temple courtyard.

summary: If blood of a korban got mixed with water, it is kosher if it still looks like blood. Wine or the blood of regular animals is looked at as if it were water. Rabbi Yehudah says blood does not cancel out blood.

chunks.en: Blood that got mixed with water,
chunks.st: In the case of blood of an offering fit for sacrifice that was mixed with water,

chunks.en: if it still looks like blood,
chunks.st: if the mixture has the appearance of blood

chunks.en: it is kosher. If it got mixed with wine,
chunks.st: it is fit for sprinkling on the altar, even though the majority of the mixture is water. If the blood was mixed with red wine,

chunks.en: we look at it as if it were water.
chunks.st: one views the wine as though it is water.
chunks.stMore: If that amount of water would leave the mixture with the appearance of blood it is fit for presentation.

chunks.he: נִתְעָרֵב בְּדַם בְּהֵמָה אוֹ בְדַם חַיָּה,
chunks.en: If it got mixed with the blood of a regular animal or a wild animal,
chunks.st: And likewise if the blood was mixed with the blood of a non-sacred domesticated animal or the blood of a non-sacred undomesticated animal,

chunks.en: we look at it as if it were water.
chunks.st: one considers the non-sacred blood as though it is water.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: blood does not cancel out blood.
chunks.st: Blood does not nullify blood.
chunks.stMore: Therefore, the priest presents the blood of the mixture on the altar.

summary: If good blood got mixed with blood of pasul korbanos, or with the weaker blood that oozes out after shechitah, it is all poured into the drain. Rabbi Eliezer says the second mix is kosher, and if the Kohen already put it on the mizbeach, it is kosher.

chunks.en: If it got mixed with the blood of pasul korbanos,
chunks.st: If blood fit for presentation was mixed with the blood of unfit offerings, there is no remedy. Therefore,

chunks.en: it is poured into the drain.
chunks.st: the entire mixture shall be poured into the drain running through the Temple courtyard. Likewise,

words.note: A water channel that ran through the courtyard.

chunks.en: With blood that oozes out,
chunks.st: if blood fit for presentation was mixed with blood of exudate,
chunks.stMore: i.e., that exudes from the neck after the initial spurt following its slaughter concludes, which is unfit for presentation,

words.note: Blood that drips out after the first strong flow at shechitah.

chunks.en: it is poured into the drain.
chunks.st: the entire mixture shall be poured into the Temple courtyard drain.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says it is kosher.
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer deems this mixture fit for presentation. Even according to the first tanna,

chunks.en: If he did not ask and put it on, it is kosher.
chunks.st: if the priest did not consult the authorities and placed the blood on the altar, the offering is fit.

words.note: He did not ask the Rabbis what to do.

summary: Blood of kosher korbanos mixed with blood of blemished animals is poured out. If one cup got mixed with other cups, Rabbi Eliezer says that once one cup was offered, all may be offered; the Sages say even the last one is poured out.

chunks.en: Blood of animals without a blemish mixed with blood of blemished animals
chunks.st: If the blood of unblemished offerings was mixed with the blood of blemished animals unfit for sacrifice,

chunks.en: is poured into the drain.
chunks.st: the entire mixture shall be poured into the Temple courtyard drain.
chunks.stMore: This is the halakha when the fit and unfit blood were mixed in one vessel. By contrast,

chunks.en: A cup mixed up with other cups,
chunks.st: if a cup of the blood of a blemished offering was intermingled with cups
chunks.stMore: of blood fit for offering and it is unclear which blood is in the cup,

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:
chunks.stMore: Although it is prohibited to present all the blood due to the uncertainty,

chunks.en: if one cup was offered,
chunks.st: if it happened that a priest already sacrificed, i.e., presented, one cup,

chunks.en: all the cups should be offered.
chunks.st: the blood in all the other cups shall be sacrificed,
chunks.stMore: as the blood that was presented is assumed to have come from the unfit cup in the mixture.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: אֲפִלּוּ קָרְבוּ כֻלָּם חוּץ מֵאַחַד מֵהֶן,
chunks.en: even if all of them were offered except for one of them,
chunks.st: Even if the blood in all the cups was sacrificed except for one of them,

chunks.en: it is poured into the drain.
chunks.st: the remaining blood shall be poured into the Temple courtyard drain.

summary: If blood that goes below the red line got mixed with blood that goes above it, Rabbi Eliezer says to put it above and then below. The Sages say to pour it out, but if he already put it on, it is kosher.

chunks.en: Blood put below that got mixed with blood put above,
chunks.st: With regard to blood that is to be placed below the red line circumscribing the altar, e.g., blood of a burnt offering, a guilt offering, or a peace offering, that was mixed with blood that is to be placed above the red line, e.g., blood of a sin offering,

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: he should put it above,
chunks.st: The priest shall initially place the blood of the mixture above the red line for the sake of the sin offering,

chunks.en: and I look at the lower blood
chunks.st: and I view the blood that was to be placed below

chunks.en: up above as if it were water,
chunks.st: that was in fact placed above as though it is water,

chunks.en: and he goes back and puts it below.
chunks.st: and the priest shall again place blood from the mixture below.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: it is poured into the drain.
chunks.st: It shall all be poured into the Temple courtyard drain. Even according to the Rabbis,

chunks.en: And if he did not ask and put it on, it is kosher.
chunks.st: if the priest did not consult the authorities and placed the blood above the red line, the offering is fit,
chunks.stMore: and he should then place the remaining blood below the red line.

summary: Blood that needs one putting mixed with blood that needs four: Rabbi Eliezer says to put it four times, and Rabbi Yehoshua says once. They argue about the mitzvos "do not add" and "do not take away" from the Torah.

chunks.en: Blood put with one putting that got mixed
chunks.st: In a case of the blood of an offering that is to be placed on the altar with one placement that was mixed with

chunks.en: with blood put with one putting,
chunks.st: the blood of another offering that is to be placed on the altar with one placement,
chunks.stMore: e.g., the blood of a firstborn offering with the blood of another firstborn offering or the blood of an animal tithe offering,

chunks.en: is put with one putting.
chunks.st: the blood shall be placed with one placement.

chunks.en: Four puttings with four puttings,
chunks.st: In a case of the blood of an offering that is to be placed on the altar with four placements that was mixed with the blood of another offering that is to be placed on the altar with four placements,
chunks.stMore: e.g., the blood of a sin offering with that of another sin offering, or the blood of a burnt offering with that of a peace offering,

chunks.en: is put with four puttings.
chunks.st: the blood shall be placed with four placements.

chunks.en: Four puttings with one putting,
chunks.st: If the blood of an offering that is to be placed on the altar with four placements was mixed with the blood of an offering that is to be placed on the altar with one placement,

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: it is put with four puttings.
chunks.st: The blood shall be placed with four placements.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua says:

chunks.en: it is put with one putting.
chunks.st: The blood shall be placed with one placement,
chunks.stMore: as the priest fulfills the requirement with one placement after the fact.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said to Rabbi Yehoshua:

chunks.he: וַהֲרֵי הוּא עוֹבֵר עַל בַּל תִּגְרַע.
chunks.en: But then he breaks the mitzvah "do not take away"!
chunks.st: According to your opinion, the priest violates the prohibition of: Do not diminish,
chunks.stMore: as it is written: “All these matters that I command you, that you shall observe to do; you shall not add thereto, nor diminish from it” (Deuteronomy 13:1). One may not diminish the number of required placements from four to one.

words.note: A mitzvah in the Torah not to take away from a mitzvah.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said to Rabbi Eliezer:

chunks.he: וַהֲרֵי הוּא עוֹבֵר עַל בַּל תּוֹסִיף.
chunks.en: But then he breaks the mitzvah "do not add"!
chunks.st: According to your opinion, the priest violates the prohibition of: Do not add,
chunks.stMore: derived from the same verse. One may not add to the one required placement and place four.

words.note: A mitzvah in the Torah not to add to a mitzvah.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said to Rabbi Yehoshua:

chunks.en: "Do not add" was said only
chunks.st: The prohibition of: Do not add, is stated only

chunks.en: when the blood is by itself.
chunks.st: in a case where the blood is by itself, not when it is part of a mixture.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said to Rabbi Eliezer:

chunks.en: "Do not take away" was said only
chunks.st: Likewise, the prohibition of: Do not diminish, is stated only

chunks.en: when the blood is by itself.
chunks.st: in a case where the blood is by itself.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Yehoshua also said,
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yehoshua also said:

chunks.en: When you put it on, you broke "do not add"
chunks.st: When you placed four placements, you transgressed the prohibition of: Do not add,

chunks.en: and you did an action with your hand.
chunks.st: and you performed a direct action.

chunks.en: And when you did not put it on,
chunks.st: When you did not place four placements but only one,

chunks.en: you broke "do not take away"
chunks.st: although you transgressed the prohibition of: Do not diminish,

chunks.en: but you did not do an action with your hand.
chunks.st: you did not perform a direct action. An active transgression is more severe than a passive one.

summary: Blood that goes inside the Heichal mixed with blood that goes outside is poured out. If it was put inside and then outside, Rabbi Akiva says it is pasul and the Sages say it is kosher; the Sages say only a chatas is pasul after it was brought inside.

chunks.he: הַנִּתָּנִין בִּפְנִים שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ עִם הַנִּתָּנִין בַּחוּץ,
chunks.en: Blood put inside that got mixed with blood put outside
chunks.st: Blood that is to be placed on three locations inside the Sanctuary, i.e., between the staves, on the Curtain, and on the golden altar, that was mixed with blood that is to be placed outside
chunks.stMore: the Sanctuary on the external altar in the Temple courtyard, has no remedy, as one may not change the location of the placement of the blood of one to fulfill his obligation with the other type of blood. Therefore,

chunks.en: is poured into the drain.
chunks.st: all the blood shall be poured into the Temple courtyard drain.

chunks.en: If he put it outside and then put it inside,
chunks.st: If the priest, on his own initiative, placed the mixture of blood outside the Sanctuary and again placed the mixture of blood inside the Sanctuary,

chunks.en: it is kosher. If inside and then he put it outside,
chunks.st: the offering is fit. If the priest, on his own initiative, placed the mixture of blood inside the Sanctuary and again placed the mixture of blood outside the Sanctuary,

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says it is pasul,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva deems the blood placed outside disqualified,

chunks.en: and the Sages say it is kosher.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis deem it fit.

chunks.en: Because Rabbi Akiva used to say,
chunks.st: As Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: all blood that came in to bring kapparah in the Heichal
chunks.st: Any blood that is to be presented outside that entered to atone in the Sanctuary

words.note: The holy building inside the courtyard.

chunks.en: is pasul. And the Sages say,
chunks.st: is disqualified; but the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: only a chatas.
chunks.st: That is the halakha with regard to the blood of an external sin offering alone,
chunks.stMore: as it is written: “And any sin offering, whereof any of the blood is brought into the Tent of Meeting to atone in the Sanctuary, shall not be eaten” (Leviticus 6:23).

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: the asham too,
chunks.st: The status of a guilt offering is like that of a sin offering as well,

chunks.en: as it says, "Like the chatas is the asham."
chunks.st: as it is stated: “As is the sin offering, so is the guilt offering”
chunks.stMore: (Leviticus 7:7), i.e., there is one halakha for them. That is not the case with regard to the blood of other offerings.

words.note: Where this pasuk is found.

summary: If the blood of a chatas was caught in two cups and one cup was taken out, the other stays kosher. If one cup was taken into the Heichal, they argue whether the other is still kosher. The tzitz of the Kohen Gadol fixes only blood that was tamei.

chunks.en: A chatas whose blood he caught in two cups,
chunks.st: In the case of a sin offering whose blood placement is on the external altar whose blood the priest collected in two cups,

chunks.en: if one of them went outside,
chunks.st: if one of them left the Temple courtyard and was thereby disqualified,

chunks.en: the one inside is kosher.
chunks.st: the cup that remained inside the courtyard is fit to be presented.

chunks.en: If one of them went inside,
chunks.st: If one of the cups entered inside the Sanctuary and was thereby disqualified,

words.note: Into the Heichal.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei HaGlili says the outside one is kosher,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili deems the blood in the cup that remained outside the Sanctuary, in the courtyard, fit to be presented,

chunks.en: and the Sages say it is pasul.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis deem it disqualified from being presented.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei HaGlili said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili said
chunks.stMore: in support of his opinion: The halakha is that if one slaughters an offering with the intent that its blood be presented outside of the Temple courtyard, the offering is disqualified, but if his intention was that the blood be presented inside the Sanctuary, the offering is not disqualified.

chunks.en: If in a place where a thought makes it pasul,
chunks.st: Just as in a case where part of the blood reached a place where the intent to present the blood there disqualifies the offering, i.e.,

chunks.he: בַּחוּץ, לֹא עָשָׂה אֶת הַמְשׁוֹאָר כַּיוֹצֵא,
chunks.en: outside, he did not make the leftover blood like the blood that went out,
chunks.st: outside the Temple courtyard, and yet when some of the blood is taken there it does not render the status of the remaining blood disqualified like that of blood that leaves the courtyard, so too,

chunks.en: then in a place where a thought does not make it pasul,
chunks.st: in a case where part of the blood reached a place where the intent to present the blood there does not disqualify the offering, i.e.,

chunks.st: inside the Sanctuary, is it not logical that we will not deem

chunks.st: the status of the remaining blood like that of blood that entered

words.en: like the one that went in

chunks.en: If it went in to bring kapparah,
chunks.st: entered the Sanctuary to atone through sprinkling,

chunks.en: even though it did not bring kapparah,
chunks.st: despite the fact that the priest did not actually sprinkle the blood to atone,

chunks.en: it is pasul, says Rabbi Eliezer.
chunks.st: the offering is disqualified; this is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: only once it brings kapparah.
chunks.st: The offering is disqualified only when he atones and sprinkles the blood in the Sanctuary.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: if he brought it in by mistake,
chunks.st: If he took the blood into the Sanctuary unwittingly,

chunks.en: it is kosher. All the pasul blood that was put
chunks.st: the blood remains fit to be presented. With regard to all the blood disqualified

chunks.en: on top of the mizbeach,
chunks.st: for presentation that was placed on the altar,

chunks.he: לֹא הִרְצָה הַצִּיץ אֶלָּא עַל הַטָּמֵא,
chunks.en: the tzitz made it accepted only for what was tamei,
chunks.st: the frontplate effects acceptance only for offerings sacrificed that are ritually impure.
chunks.stMore: Although it is written with regard to the frontplate worn on the forehead of the High Priest: “And it shall be upon Aaron’s forehead, and Aaron shall bear the iniquity committed in the sacred matters” (Exodus 28:38), this does not apply to all disqualifications of offerings.

words.note: The gold band on the forehead of the Kohen Gadol.

chunks.en: because the tzitz makes things accepted for what is tamei,
chunks.st: This is because the frontplate effects acceptance for offerings sacri-ficed that are ritually impure

chunks.en: but it does not make accepted what went outside.
chunks.st: but does not effect acceptance for offerings that leave the courtyard.
